annotations.keyFindings: Across six hospitals, reports containing all key elements rose from 64 to 91 percent after templates; sign-off time rose by a median of 2 minutes; 88 percent template use at six months.
annotations.limitations: Before-after; checklist designed with the template.

annotations.keyFindings: Template opened for 94 percent, fully completed for 71 percent, overridden in 23 percent; use plateaued at four months.
Structured reports were more complete in 27 of 32 studies and referrer satisfaction higher in 9 of 11; no patient outcomes measured.
Referrers valued appendix diameter, free fluid and gas, and a one-line impression; long reports reduced usefulness.
Kappa 0.72 for rating free-text reports against the new checklist; a stated-or-clearly-implied rule raised measured completeness by 9 points.
annotations.notes: Needed for a fair historic comparison.

annotations.keyFindings: Active reporting time rose by 1.4 minutes in the first month and returned to baseline by month four; oncology staging stayed about one minute longer.

claims.text: After structured templates were introduced in six hospitals, reports containing all key elements rose from 64 to 91 percent.
claims.passage: The proportion of reports containing all pre-specified key elements for the clinical question rose from 64 to 91 percent.
claims.interpretation: A large completeness gain is plausible here.

claims.text: In one department, the template was fully completed for 71 percent of reports and overridden with free text in 23 percent.
claims.passage: fully completed for 71 percent; in 23 percent a radiologist overrode the template with free text for at least one section
claims.interpretation: Template use must be defined as completion without override.

claims.text: Counting elements as present when stated or clearly implied raised measured completeness of free-text reports by 9 percentage points.
claims.passage: Applying a rule that counted an element as present when it was stated or clearly implied raised measured completeness of free-text reports by 9 percentage points.
claims.interpretation: The historic comparison needs this rule fixed in advance.

synthesis: Six retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Structured templates were followed by more complete reports in a multicentre study (64 to 91 percent) and in most studies in a systematic review, with higher referrer satisfaction where measured. Adoption plateaus after about four months, with overrides common among senior radiologists, and reporting time rises briefly before returning to baseline. Historic free-text reports need a stated-or-implied rule to be compared fairly.
gradeRationale: Consistent completeness gains across a multicentre study and a systematic review of 32 studies, downgraded for before-after designs and checklists designed with templates; certainty for reporting time and referrer views is lower.
summary: Six retrieved records appraised; three claims recorded; overall certainty moderate for completeness.
